simple.meaning: מָלוֹן (mâlôwn) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a lodgment , i.e. caravanserai or encampment.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 42:27. The surrounding context includes priesthood, mountain, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מָלוֹן (H4411) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: מָלוֹן (mâlôwn) / H4411 is traced through Genesis 42:27, Genesis 43:21, Exodus 4:24, Joshua 4:3 with generated occurrence evidence.

structuredEvidence.definition: a lodgment , i.e. caravanserai or encampment

firstOccurrence.englishText: As one of them opened his sack to give his donkey food in the lodging place, he saw his money. Behold, it was in the mouth of his sack.

timeline.evidenceText: As one of them opened his sack to give his donkey food in the lodging place, he saw his money. Behold, it was in the mouth of his sack.
When we came to the lodging place, we opened our sacks, and behold, each man’s money was in the mouth of his sack, our money in full weight. We have brought it back in our hand.
On the way at a lodging place, Yahweh met Moses and wanted to kill him.

and command them, saying, ‘Take from out of the middle of the Jordan, out of the place where the priests’ feet stood firm, twelve stones, carry them over with you, and lay them down in the place where you’ll camp tonight.’ ”

The children of Israel did as Joshua commanded, and took up twelve stones out of the middle of the Jordan, as Yahweh spoke to Joshua, according to the number of the tribes of the children of Israel. They carried them over with them to the place where they camped, and laid them down there.

By your messengers, you have defied the Lord, and have said, “With the multitude of my chariots, I have come up to the height of the mountains, to the innermost parts of Lebanon, and I will cut down its tall cedars and its choice cypress trees; and I will enter into his farthest lodging place, the forest of his fruitful field.
They have gone over the pass. They have taken up their lodging at Geba. Ramah trembles. Gibeah of Saul has fled.
Oh that my head were waters,

definitions.full: H4411. malon מָלוֺן noun masculine lodging-place, inn, khan ; — absolute ׳מ Gen 42:27 5 t.; construct מְלוֺן 2Kin 19:23 ; Jer 9:1 ; — lodging-place, inn, khan (?) Gen 42:27 ; 43:21 ; Exod 4:24 ; ׳מְ אֹרְתִים Jer 9:1 ; = camp (of Israel) for a night, Josh 4:3 ( + לין ), 4:8 ; of Assyrians Isa 10:29 ; figurative קִצֹּה֯ מְלוֺן 2Kin 19:23 , i.e. its (Lebanon's) remotest camping-ground, hyperb. of Assyrian conquest; so read probably in || Isa 37:24 for ק ׳מְרוֺם ᵑ0 , compare Di Du Kit Che Hpt .
